questions.q: I've never done reformer. Where do I start?
questions.a: Foundation. It's built for a first time, and your teacher shows you the reformer before anything moves.
Leggings or shorts you can move in, and socks with grips. We sell grip socks at the desk.

questions.q: How many people are in a class?
questions.a: Six at most: there are six reformers.

questions.q: Do I need to be fit or flexible?
questions.a: No. The springs are set for you, lighter or heavier, and Foundation goes slowly.

questions.q: Can I come if I'm pregnant?
questions.a: Yes, to Pre & postnatal, from fourteen weeks and with your GP's or midwife's go-ahead. Tell your teacher how far along you are.

questions.q: I have an injury. Is it safe?
questions.a: Tell us before you book. Often a private session first is best, so we can see how you move.

questions.q: What if I can't make it?
questions.a: Cancel twelve hours before and the class goes back on your card. Later than that, it's used.

questions.q: What if a class is full?
questions.a: Tap Waitlist. If a reformer frees up, we message you.
One shower and a changing room with lockers, towels and hairdryers.
Yes: class cards, private sessions or any amount. Written by hand.
It depends how often you'll come: the calculator on the classes page works it out.

method.title: The method
method.intro: Six moves you'll meet in your first month, in our words.

items.name: Mermaid
items.line: A long side stretch, kneeling or sitting.
items.text: Sitting side-on, one hand on the footbar, you push the carriage away and reach the other arm over your head.
items.works: The sides of your body, your shoulders, the spine's ability to bend sideways
items.easier: Keep the reach small and the hand lower on the bar
items.harder: Kneel instead of sitting, and add a twist at the end

photo.alt: A woman kneels side-on to the reformer, one hand on the bar, the other arm reaching over

items.name: Leg springs
items.line: Lying down, legs in the springs of the tower.
items.text: Lying on the mat of the tower, feet in the loops, you press down against the springs and let them bring you back, slowly.
items.works: Inner thighs, the backs of the legs, the deep core holding you still
items.springs: On the tower: springs set by your teacher
items.easier: Bend the knees and keep the circles small
items.harder: Bigger circles, and lift the head and shoulders

photo.alt: A woman lies on the tower, legs raised in the springs

items.name: Feet in straps
items.line: On your back, feet in the straps, legs moving together.
items.text: Lying on the carriage with the straps round your feet, you bend and stretch your legs, open and close them, and draw circles.
items.works: The backs of the legs, the hips, the inner thighs
items.springs: Medium: one red and one blue
items.easier: Keep the knees soft and the range short
items.harder: Lift the hips into a bridge between sets

photo.alt: A woman lies on the reformer, legs raised in the straps

items.name: Standing lunge
items.line: One foot on the frame, one on the carriage.
items.text: Standing beside the reformer with one foot on the platform and one against the shoulder rest, you lunge the carriage out and draw it back in.
items.works: Glutes, the fronts of the thighs, balance
items.easier: Hold the frame with one hand and keep the lunge short
items.harder: Arms overhead, then lower the back knee nearly to the carriage

photo.alt: Three women lunge on their reformers, arms reaching forward

items.name: Teaser
items.line: Balancing on the sit bones, legs and arms long.
items.text: From lying, you roll up into a V, arms reaching for your feet, and roll back down one bone at a time.
items.works: The deep and outer abdominals, the hip flexors, control
items.springs: On the mat, or with a light spring for help
items.easier: Keep the knees bent and the feet down
items.harder: Hold a weighted ball, or pass it to a partner

photo.alt: A woman and a man balance in a teaser on mats, passing a weighted ball

items.name: Pelvic curl
items.line: Lying down, peeling the spine off the carriage.
items.text: Feet on the footbar, you curl your hips up one bone at a time, hold, and roll back down.
items.works: Glutes, the backs of the legs, the spine's movement
items.easier: Keep the curl low and the carriage still
items.harder: Push the carriage out and in while the hips are up

photo.alt: A teacher steadies a client's knees as she curls her hips up on the reformer

prenatal.title: Pregnancy and after
prenatal.intro: Which class when, and what changes.
prenatal.goAhead: Before you come, get the go-ahead from your GP or midwife, and tell us how far along you are each time. If anything feels wrong in a class, stop: your teacher will adapt it.
prenatal.message: Hello Ottoline, I'm pregnant and have a question about classes.

photo.alt: A pregnancy class stretches over exercise balls

stages.text: Keep coming to the classes you know, if you already practise; tell your teacher, who'll lighten the springs and leave out deep twists. New to the reformer? Wait until 14 weeks.
Pre & postnatal: side-lying and seated work, nothing flat on your back, breathing and the pelvic floor.
The same class, gentler. Many stop around 36 weeks; your teacher and midwife decide with you.
Back in Pre & postnatal once your GP has seen you. After a caesarean, usually later: ask first.
Foundation, then the rest of the timetable when your teacher agrees.
